name: graphsearch
description: Search the corpus using the original query and any complementary queries. Acquire retrieved and path documents. Return each query branch’s Top10 source IDs, titles, availability, shared-entity paths, and short relevant raw passages. Full Maps are also saved in .cep/MAP.txt. Later search is a fallback for a gap that current sources cannot resolve.

queries.description: A nonempty list of natural-language corpus queries. Combine complementary formulations in this list. This is the only argument accepted by graphsearch.

name: read
description: Read an acquired file or saved tool output. Use the returned path and character window, or offset/limit for lines. Output is capped at 10 KiB. Read further context only when needed to interpret the evidence.

path.description: The exact acquired file path. For source_id=12345 in the Map, use .cep/s/12345.txt.

offset.description: Starting line number, beginning at 1. Omit to start at the beginning.

limit.description: Number of lines to read. Include enough context to interpret the passage.

charOffset.description: Zero-based character offset for a window inside a long text file.

charLimit.description: Maximum characters to return with charOffset; default 4096.

byteOffset.description: Zero-based byte offset for a bounded window.

byteLimit.description: Maximum bytes to return with byteOffset; default 4096.

name: bash
description: Run a command in the workspace. Use rg -nH to locate evidence in acquired files. Titles and source IDs are listed in .cep/catalogue.tsv. Long matches retain excerpts and read-window hints. Output is capped at 10 KiB and full output is saved.

command.description: A Bash command run in the workspace. Acquired documents are in .cep/s/. python3 is available.

timeout.description: Optional command execution time limit, measured in seconds. This argument is specific to bash.

name: graphexpand
description: Search the two-hop graph neighborhood of an IN or OUT source for the missing fact described by query. Acquire the anchor and retrieved/path documents. Return the anchor separately and up to ten ranked related sources with shared-entity paths, relevant raw passages, and read windows. Results can reveal new sources or highlight evidence already acquired.

source_id.description: Numeric source_id copied from the Map or catalogue, written as a string.

query.description: The missing fact or relationship to seek near the starting document. If omitted, the original question is used.
